breakfast.name: Akwadu (Baked Banana)
instructions: Halve bananas, place in dish
Mix sugar, orange juice, coconut
Pour over bananas, dot with butter
Bake at 180°C 20 min
breakfast.description: Baked bananas glazed with orange and coconut.

breakfast.name: Fried Plantains with Eggs
instructions: Slice and fry plantains
Scramble or fry eggs
Serve together
breakfast.description: Simple breakfast of fried plantains and eggs.

breakfast.name: Akwadu (Baked Banana with Coconut)
instructions: Peel ripe plantains, halve lengthwise
Melt butter in baking dish
Arrange plantain halves, drizzle with orange juice
Mix coconut cream, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg — pour over
Bake at 175°C for 20 min until plantains are soft and golden
The coconut cream caramelizes into a sweet, fragrant sauce
Serve warm as breakfast or dessert — it works for both
breakfast.description: Baked plantains in caramelized coconut cream — Equatorial Guinea's sweet, comforting breakfast or dessert. The simplicity of the tropical ingredients (plantain, coconut, citrus) and the caramelization make this a viral example of Central African tropical cooking at its most elegant.

lunch.name: Succotash Equatoguineano
instructions: Cook corn and beans
Sauté onion and tomatoes in palm oil
Add corn, beans, and fish
Season with chili, simmer 15 min
lunch.description: Corn and bean stew with smoked fish.

lunch.name: Pepesoup (Spicy Fish Soup)
instructions: Boil fish with tomatoes, onion, pepper
Simmer 20 min
Add basil and lime juice
Serve hot

lunch.name: Succotash de Mariscos (Seafood Stew)
ingredients: Mixed seafood: shrimp, crab, fish (whatever's fresh)
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic in palm oil until fragrant
Add tomatoes, cook down into sauce
Add coconut milk and bring to simmer
Add firmer fish first, then shrimp and crab — don't overcook the shrimp
Add sliced okra and ripe plantain chunks
Season with Scotch bonnet, salt, Maggi
Simmer until everything is tender and sauce is thick
Serve over rice or with boiled plantain
Bioko Island's seafood tradition — the Gulf of Guinea delivers daily
lunch.description: Equatorial Guinea's Gulf of Guinea seafood stew — a rich coconut-and-palm-oil broth loaded with whatever the fishermen brought in that day. The island of Bioko's coastal cooking tradition combines African and Spanish influences in one of Central Africa's most underexplored cuisines.

dinner.name: Chicken in Peanut Sauce
instructions: Brown chicken, set aside
Sauté onion, garlic, tomatoes
Add peanut butter and water
Return chicken, simmer 30 min

dinner.name: Bambara (Stewed Beans)
instructions: Cook beans until tender
Add palm oil, onion, tomatoes, fish
Simmer 20 min
dinner.description: Black-eyed peas stewed with palm oil and smoked fish.

dinner.name: Pepesoup (Spicy Pepper Soup)
ingredients: Pepesoup spice: calabash nutmeg (ehuru), alligator pepper, uziza, uda
instructions: Boil goat meat with onion until tender — 30-40 min
Add all pepesoup spices — these are the unique aromatics that define the dish
Add Scotch bonnet for heat, garlic, ginger
Simmer another 15 min — the broth becomes intensely aromatic and peppery
Add scent leaves at the very end — just wilt them
The broth should be thin and intensely spiced, not thick
Serve hot in bowls — this is restorative food, the African penicillin
Drink the broth, eat the meat with your hands
dinner.description: The 'African penicillin' — an intensely spiced, thin goat broth made with rare aromatics like calabash nutmeg and alligator pepper. Restorative, fiery, and deeply fragrant. Pepesoup has gone viral as the ultimate cold-and-flu remedy from West and Central Africa.

snacks.name: Empanadas de Plátano
instructions: Boil and mash plantains
Fill with cooked seasoned beef
Shape and fry until golden

snacks.name: Croquetas de Pescado (Fish Croquettes)
instructions: Make thick béchamel: melt butter, add flour, cook, add milk gradually — it must be very thick
Mix in flaked fish, sautéed onion, garlic, parsley, nutmeg
Spread in a tray, refrigerate until firm — at least 2 hours
Shape into cylinders
Dip in egg wash, then breadcrumbs
Deep fry at 170°C until golden and crispy — about 3 min
Inside should be creamy, outside shattering
This is the Spanish colonial influence — croquetas are everywhere in Malabo
snacks.description: Spanish-style fish croquettes from Equatorial Guinea — crispy outside, creamy fish béchamel inside. The Spanish colonial culinary legacy meets Gulf of Guinea seafood. Malabo's tapas bars serve these as the bridge between African and Iberian cuisine.

desserts.name: Coconut Flan
instructions: Caramelize sugar in mold
Blend eggs, milks, vanilla
Pour into mold
Bake in water bath at 160°C 45 min
Chill and unmold

desserts.name: Plátano Frito con Chocolate (Fried Plantain with Chocolate)
instructions: Slice ripe plantains diagonally into thick pieces
Fry in hot oil until deeply caramelized and golden — 3-4 min per side
Drain briefly
Drizzle with melted dark chocolate
Sprinkle with sea salt and crushed peanuts
The sweet-salty-bitter combination is addictive
This is Equatorial Guinea's twist on fried plantain — the chocolate comes from the cacao that grows on the islands
desserts.description: Fried ripe plantain drizzled with dark chocolate and sea salt — Equatorial Guinea grows cacao on its islands, making this a truly local dessert. The caramelized plantain-and-chocolate combination has gone viral as an African-chocolate origin story.

drinks.name: Malamba (Sugarcane Liquor)
instructions: Press sugarcane
Ferment juice 5-7 days
Distill

drinks.name: Topé (Palm Wine)
instructions: Tap palm tree
Collect sap
Serve fresh same day
